REIGN OF THE WEREDRAGON
VILLAIN BUILDER
Cut out the prompts, fold them up, randomly select fifteen
prompts, and place them on the table within reach of everyone
participating. Go around the table, starting with the player to
your left. On each player’s turn, they grab a prompt, read it
aloud, then answer the question. Other players may follow up
with additional questions, though the player with the prompt
doesn’t need to answer them.
The queen once ordered the creation of
something beautiful in her honor. What
was it, and where does it now reside?
Forlorne holds an annual celebration in her
own honor.  What does she require from
citizens during the event, and how are
they punished if they refuse to comply?
What is a unique or unexpected
part of Forlorne’s appearance that
affects how people view her?
Forlorne and one of the Knights of Whelvia
are rumored to be having an affair. Who is
the knight, and what are they known for?
What heinous acts has Forlorne imposed
upon her citizens since becoming queen?
Forlorne recently quashed a small rebellion.
Who led that effort, and what mistake did
they make that led to their downfall?
Forlorne frequently visits a remote
Whelvian village. Why do the locals
believe she keeps coming back?
The queen’s regime has taken many people
from their homes. Why were these people
chosen, and where does Forlorne send them?
The queen recently lost a close member
of her royal court. Who were they, and
how has she responded to their death?
Daggerheart © Darrington Press 2026

If the player chooses a prompt they would rather not answer,
or would prefer somebody else answer instead, they can
always pass it to that player or discard it from play. When
there are no more prompts to answer, continue to character
creation.
What unique magical item is Forlorne
rumored to seek? What are people
afraid she’ll do if she gets it?
What inoffensive item, symbol, or practice
did Forlorne ban when she came to
power? What is the punishment for those
who are caught violating the ban?
What defensive systems are rumored
to protect the fortress of Nwarlyth
where Forlorne resides?
Who is the queen’s most recently appointed
royal advisor, and what aspect of the
kingdom are they responsible for?
What is the Whelvians’ nickname for
Forlorne, and where did it come from?
The queen’s favorite weapon once
belonged to someone else. What is
it, and who owned it previously?
Which Whelvian hero vocally
supports Forlorne? How does
she reward them?
What distinct markings, patterns, or
features do Forlorne’s weredrakes
bear once she transforms them?
The queen has a childhood friend who’s
now a member of her court. Who are
they, and what’s strange about them?

REIGN OF THE WEREDRAGON
villain builder
What creature does the queen keep chained in
her dungeon, and why does she keep it alive?
One member of Forlorne’s royal court is
treated differently from the others. Why is that,
and how do the other nobles feel about it?
What trait or behavior of others
brings out Forlorne’s cruelty?
Forlorne recently destroyed something
vital to many Whelvians. What happened,
and who has been most affected?
What act of kindness did Forlorne
recently commit? What controversy
has come about because of it?
A foreign leader recently asked Forlorne
for her hand in marriage, hoping to
forge a powerful alliance. Who were
they, and how did Forlorne respond?
Forlorne meets her sky seers in a very
specific place. Where do they go, and
why does she bring them there?
What symbol do followers of the queen use
to identify themselves to one another?
Forlorne elevated someone to power who
was an unexpected choice. Who are they, and
why do people believe she chose them?
Forlorne recently killed a sky seer.
What did this person see in the night
sky that caused her to kill them?
Which criminal organization handles
clandestine tasks for the queen?
Daggerheart © Darrington Press 2026

What scandalous story is everyone
telling from Forlorne’s last grand ball?
Forlorne sometimes disappears from
Whelvia for short stretches of time.
Where do people say she goes?
Someone saved the queen’s life. Who
were they, and what happened?
Forlorne’s castle contains a secret
room that only she can access.
What does she hide there?
What promises has Forlorne made to
the people of Whelvia, and what, if any,
action has she taken to fulfill them?
Forlorne is demonizing a specific community,
blaming them for Whelvia’s problems.
Which community is it, and what has she
tasked her knights to do in response?
What specific claims does the
queen’s most recent propaganda
campaign make to her people?
What symbol do Whelvian rebels use to
identify themselves to one another?
What new process has Forlorne
implemented to dispatch those she
deems criminal in Whelvia?
What did Forlorne say at her last
widely attended speech? How
did the audience react?
What is the queen’s rumored vice, and
where in Whelvia does she go to satisfy it?

JOURNEY TO HORIZON
doom track

The Doom Track represents growing disasters that befall New Valloren if
the party doesn’t resurrect Aurelia. At the end of each session, mark a box
from the party’s tier or below. You can’t mark a nested box until you mark
the box it’s nested under.

Tier 1: dark HARBINGERS
Tier 2: rising threats

After you mark 5 boxes in this tier, when you gain Fear at the end of a
long rest, you roll twice and take the higher result.
	 Bandits and marauders harry travelers.
	 Tensions rise over contested resources.
	 A mysteriously empty sanctuary is discovered.
	 A sanctuary seals itself off once again.
	 A new settlement is overtaken by surging wilderness.
	 Chimeric dire beasts reveal their presence.
	 Swarms of overgrown insects darken the sky.
	 Wild magic shatters magic and crumbles stone.
	 Terrana supercharges magic dangerously and unpredictably.
	 A shadowblighted orchard turns to ash overnight.
	 Desiccated and blackened birds fall dead from the sky.
	 Shadowblighted echoes of lost loved ones appear.
	 Travelers trade stories of Seeker sightings.
	 The party suffers visions of the Lovers’ re-emergence.
	 An Aurelian shrine lies broken and desecrated.
	 The party finds signs of a Seeker.
	 The party finds remnants of a cult ritual.
	 A cultist spy tracks the party.
	 The Vessel attracts attention—and suspicion.

After you mark 5 boxes in this tier, when you generate a region and the
result on the d20 is a 1, treat it as if you’d rolled 1 twice in a row.
	 Roving bands of professional soldiers demand tribute at swordpoint.
	 A demagogue rises to power with promises of prosperity.
	 A noble demands fealty from their neighbors.
	 A prominent figure in the Aurelian Order persecutes the unfaithful.
	 Civilians are drafted in preparation for war.
	 Chaotic weather kills the harvest.
	 Tidal waves and tornadoes batter Valloren.
	 Dire beasts and walking carnivorous plants attack.
	 A fungal plague spreads through the land.
	 Food stores are spoiled by pestilence.
	 The ground cracks open, releasing a toxic miasma.
	 Shadowblight swamps a sanctuary, trapping its inhabitants.
	 A reservoir’s water turns into tar.
	 Sorrowblighted humanoids emerge from hidden settlements.
	 A Seeker crosses the party’s path.
	 An irreplaceable repository of Old Valloren knowledge is destroyed.
	 Numerous Aurelian priests are slain in a coordinated attack.
	 A Seeker chases the party, forcing them to flee.
	 An enemy discovers the Vessel’s true nature.

Tier 3: imminent destruction
Tier 4: final cataclysm

After you mark 5 boxes in this tier, adversaries gain the following feature:
Dark-Hearted - Passive: Spend a Fear to give the adversary advantage on
its next roll.
	 War is declared, and each sanctuary is called to claim a side.
	 A sanctuary falls to internal strife.
	 A vast military force sweeps through the continent.
	 A sanctuary is besieged, then falls to military force.
	 An explosion of verdant abundance renders regions impassable.
	 An ancient creature awakens from millennia of dreamless slumber.
	 Unleashed terrana drives people into animalistic fury.
	 Spellcasting triggers magical exhaustion.
	 Beasts of legend leave their lairs to terrorize the population.
	 Color drains from the world.
	 Victims of the Long Sorrow crawl from their graves.
	 Entire fields, forests, jungles, and wetlands fall to rot.
	 Unrestrained shadowblight triggers inescapable despair.
	 A Seeker corners the party, forcing them to fight.
	 A powerful personage reveals their Cult allegiance.
	 A defeated Seeker reappears with newfound abilities or allies.
	 An army of cultists sweeps across Valloren culling sanctuaries.
	 The Vessel is lost or stolen.

Each time you mark a box from this tier, you gain a number of Fear equal
to the number of marked boxes in this tier.
	 A group of Seekers ambushes the party.
	 Valloren is riven by an impassable mire of shadowblight.
	 A tyrant claims the crown of Valloren.
	 An assassin mortally wounds a party member.
	 In pockets of reality, time warps and bends in on itself.
	 A wave of wild magic sweeps across the continent, transforming
everything it touches into overgrown, uncanny forms.
	 Whole sanctuaries are terrorized by colossal agents
of the earth, raging at its exploitation.
	 The sky turns black forever, plunging Valloren into endless midnight.
	 One by one, sanctuaries slip under the surface
of an infinite sea of shadowblight.
	 The veil of death is torn asunder, spewing shambling
corpses and unclean spirits into the mortal realm.
	 The Lovers awaken and begin weaving the Second Sorrow.
	 The Vessel is destroyed.
